layer-1.title: Building an 8-bit Breadboard Computer: From Logic Gates to Register Transfers
layer-1.speaker: Ben Eater
layer-1.keyTakeaway: How physical electrical voltage levels and silicon NAND gates compose into registers, ALUs, and the fundamental machine cycle.

layer-2.title: What Has My Compiler Done for Me Lately? Unbolting the Compiler's Lid
layer-2.speaker: Matt Godbolt
layer-2.keyTakeaway: How modern compilers lower high-level constructs into assembly, registers, pipeline scheduling, and CPU cache lines.

layer-3.title: Data-Oriented Design and C++: Cache Lines, Memory Hierarchy & Hardware Reality
layer-3.speaker: Mike Acton
layer-3.keyTakeaway: Software is data transformation. Hardware latency is governed by cache line transfers and memory layout, not abstract hierarchies.

layer-4.title: Operating Systems: Architecture, Syscalls, and Kernel Substrates
layer-4.speaker: Bryan Cantrill
layer-4.keyTakeaway: How the OS kernel arbitrates hardware interrupts, virtual address translation (TLB/MMU), and process execution isolation.

layer-5.title: Function Call Mechanics: Stacks, Calling Conventions & Activation Records
layer-5.speaker: Dan Saks
layer-5.keyTakeaway: The concrete mechanics of calling conventions, prologue/epilogue generation, stack frames, return address safety, and indirect jump tables.

layer-6.title: Propositions as Types: The Curry-Howard Isomorphism & Foundations of Type Systems
layer-6.speaker: Philip Wadler
layer-6.keyTakeaway: Programs are proofs and types are propositions. Computation is not an arbitrary invention, but an inherent mathematical discovery.

layer-7.title: Concurrency is not Parallelism: Structural Composition vs Multi-Core Execution
layer-7.speaker: Rob Pike
layer-7.keyTakeaway: Concurrency is about dealing with lots of things at once; parallelism is about doing lots of things at once. How CSP structures complexity.

layer-8.title: Inventing on Principle: The Immediate Feedback Loop of Ideas and Mediums
layer-8.speaker: Bret Victor
layer-8.keyTakeaway: Creators need an immediate connection to what they're making. The ultimate purpose of language ergonomics is bridging human intent to computation.

prog_paradigms_functional_fp.title: Simple Made Easy: State, Complexity & Functional Composition
prog_paradigms_functional_fp.speaker: Rich Hickey
prog_paradigms_functional_fp.keyTakeaway: Simplicity is about disentangling concerns. Pure functions and immutable values eliminate stateful interleaving and cognitive overload.

prog_paradigms_object-oriented_oop.title: The Computer Revolution Hasn't Happened Yet: Real OOP & Late Binding
prog_paradigms_object-oriented_oop.speaker: Alan Kay
prog_paradigms_object-oriented_oop.keyTakeaway: OOP was conceived as independent biological cells communicating via messages, not as rigid class inheritance trees.

prog_paradigms_declarative.title: The Value of Values: Declarative Computing & Immutable Facts
prog_paradigms_declarative.speaker: Rich Hickey
prog_paradigms_declarative.keyTakeaway: Facts about the world are immutable. Declarative systems compute answers over sets of facts rather than performing destructive in-place mutation.

prog_paradigms_actor_model.title: The Actor Model of Computation: Scalable Robust Information Systems
prog_paradigms_actor_model.speaker: Carl Hewitt
prog_paradigms_actor_model.keyTakeaway: Actors maintain private state and communicate solely via asynchronous messages, removing the need for shared-memory locks.

prog_types_static_vs_dynamic.title: Ideology: Dynamic vs Static Typing in Real Engineering
prog_types_static_vs_dynamic.speaker: Gary Bernhardt
prog_types_static_vs_dynamic.keyTakeaway: The practical trade-offs between compile-time machine proofs and runtime dynamism at system boundaries.

prog_types_strong_vs_weak.title: Parse, Don't Validate: Enforcing Invariants via Types
prog_types_strong_vs_weak.speaker: Alexis King
prog_types_strong_vs_weak.keyTakeaway: Validate and parse input data at system boundaries so invalid states become structurally unrepresentable internally.

prog_types_hindley-milner_inference.title: Type Inference: How Hindley-Milner and Algorithm W Deduce Types
prog_types_hindley-milner_inference.speaker: Simon Peyton Jones
prog_types_hindley-milner_inference.keyTakeaway: Unification algorithms systematically deduce principal types across entire expressions without requiring manual annotations.

prog_types_dependent_types.title: Type-Driven Development with Dependent Types
prog_types_dependent_types.speaker: Edwin Brady
prog_types_dependent_types.keyTakeaway: Allowing types to depend on values turns the type-checker into an interactive theorem prover guaranteeing invariants at compile time.

prog_types_generics___polymorphism.title: Making Ad-Hoc Polymorphism Less Ad Hoc: The Theory of Type Classes
prog_types_generics___polymorphism.speaker: Philip Wadler
prog_types_generics___polymorphism.keyTakeaway: How parametric polymorphism contrasts with ad-hoc trait overloading, and how dictionary passing lowers to machine instructions.

prog_memory_manual_malloc_free.title: Memory Allocation Strategies: Arenas, Free Lists & Cache Efficiency
prog_memory_manual_malloc_free.speaker: Ginger Bill
prog_memory_manual_malloc_free.keyTakeaway: General malloc/free causes fragmentation and metadata overhead; arena allocators provide O(1) allocation and zero-cost bulk reclamation.

prog_memory_garbage_collection_gc.title: JVM Garbage Collection: The Generational Hypothesis & Modern Collectors
prog_memory_garbage_collection_gc.speaker: Aleksey Shipilëv
prog_memory_garbage_collection_gc.keyTakeaway: The generational hypothesis: most allocations die young. Segregating young and old objects optimizes collection throughput and pause times.

prog_memory_tracing_gc___mark-sweep.title: Concurrent Tracing GC: Tri-Color Marking and Barrier Invariants
prog_memory_tracing_gc___mark-sweep.speaker: Aleksey Shipilëv
prog_memory_tracing_gc___mark-sweep.keyTakeaway: How modern concurrent collectors (ZGC/Shenandoah) avoid stop-the-world pauses using load/store barriers and tri-color invariants.

prog_memory_reference_counting.title: Leak-Freedom in C++... By Default: Smart Pointers and Reference Counts
prog_memory_reference_counting.speaker: Herb Sutter
prog_memory_reference_counting.keyTakeaway: Deterministic resource reclamation with unique and shared ownership semantics, and resolving reference cycles with weak pointers.

prog_memory_ownership___borrowing_raii.title: Memory Safety Without Garbage Collection: Rust's Ownership & Borrowing
prog_memory_ownership___borrowing_raii.speaker: Niko Matsakis & Aaron Turon
prog_memory_ownership___borrowing_raii.keyTakeaway: Affine types enforce aliasing XOR mutability at compile time. Memory safety is achieved with zero runtime garbage collection overhead.

prog_concurrency_threads___mutexes.title: Threads and Locks: Lock-Free Programming and Memory Models
prog_concurrency_threads___mutexes.speaker: Herb Sutter
prog_concurrency_threads___mutexes.keyTakeaway: Hardware instruction reordering and multi-core memory models require strict synchronization fences and mutex invariants.

prog_concurrency_coroutines_async_await.title: Generators and Coroutines: Stackless Asynchronous Execution
prog_concurrency_coroutines_async_await.speaker: David Beazley
prog_concurrency_coroutines_async_await.keyTakeaway: Compiling async functions into stackless cooperative state machines that pause and resume without thread blocking.

prog_concurrency_channels___csp.title: Go Concurrency Patterns: Communicating Sequential Processes in Practice
prog_concurrency_channels___csp.speaker: Rob Pike
prog_concurrency_channels___csp.keyTakeaway: Do not communicate by sharing memory; instead, share memory by communicating. Channel rendezvous as a first-class control flow primitive.

prog_concurrency_event_loop_node_v8.title: What the Heck Is the Event Loop Anyway?
prog_concurrency_event_loop_node_v8.speaker: Philip Roberts
prog_concurrency_event_loop_node_v8.keyTakeaway: The browser and runtime execution architecture: call stack, non-blocking APIs, task queues, and the microtask drain loop.
